note.note:
Action Plan:
1) Avoid triggers: Wear protective gloves at all times when cleaning and minimize direct contact with cleaning chemicals and wet work.
2) Start topical corticosteroid cream for inflamed hand dermatitis (specific product/dose/route/frequency not documented).
3) Use a stronger emollient: Apply generously to hands 3–4 times daily for the next 10–14 days to improve dryness and skin barrier.
4) Follow-up: If no improvement after 10–14 days, or if symptoms worsen/spread, return sooner for reassessment and possible adjustment of treatment.
5) Prescription: Sent electronically to the patient’s pharmacy as discussed.
6) Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Chief concern: Painful, cracked, itchy skin on the palms of both hands for 3–4 months; worsening to the point of hindering work.
- Symptoms/details:
  - Location: Palms primarily.
  - Features: Dryness, fissuring/cracking, intermittent itch; bleeding only when scratched (no spontaneous bleeding).
  - Severity/impact: Unable to work the past 3 days due to pain.
  - Associated: Mild generalized dryness (e.g., legs), longstanding, not severe.
  - Negatives: No fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms; appetite and general well-being maintained.
- Triggers/Context:
  - Occupational exposure as a hotel housekeeper with frequent use of cleaning products; inconsistent glove use.
  - Job change about 4 months ago preceding symptom onset.
- Treatments tried: E45 emollient (no benefit); oral antihistamine (no benefit).
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug or general allergies.
- Social history: Housekeeper at a hotel; nonsmoker; alcohol “a couple of pints a week.”

Objective:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical exam: Not documented (teleconsultation; no visual exam findings provided).
- Investigations: None discussed or performed.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Painful, cracked, itchy palms consistent with hand dermatitis:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Irritant contact hand dermatitis (High) [from DDx].
   - Differential diagnosis (consistent with DDx):
     - Allergic contact dermatitis to occupational agents (Medium): pruritus and occupational exposures support; no specific allergen identified.
     - Asteatotic/xerotic eczema (Medium): baseline dryness and diabetes may impair barrier; localization and temporal link favor irritant etiology.
     - Dyshidrotic eczema (Low-Medium): lacks typical vesicles.
     - Tinea manuum (Low): lacks classic unilateral scaling or associated tinea pedis.
   - Investigations planned: None today.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Avoid irritants; wear gloves consistently when cleaning and limit wet work exposure.
     - Start topical corticosteroid cream (specific product/dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Stronger emollient: apply liberally 3–4 times daily for 10–14 days.
     - Follow-up in 10–14 days; return sooner if worsening or spreading.
   - Relevant referrals: None discussed.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: No vitals; no hands/skin exam description (erythema, scale, vesicles, distribution, laterality); no specific steroid name/potency or emollient product documented; medication doses/frequencies not documented; vaccination status not discussed.
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Occasional inaudible/garbled segments, but core clinical details and plan are clear.
